personality.usageZh: 可数名词（指具体人的性格）或不可数名词（泛指性格）。常见搭配：have a strong personality（个性很强）、personality test（性格测试）、split personality（人格分裂）。

examples.sentence: My sister has a friendly personality and everyone likes her.
examples.trans: 我姐姐性格友好，大家都喜欢她。

examples.sentence: His quiet personality makes him a good listener in our group.
examples.trans: 他安静的性格使他成为我们小组里很好的倾听者。

examples.sentence: Although the twins look the same, their personalities are completely different.
examples.trans: 虽然这对双胞胎长得一样，但他们的性格完全不同。

examples.sentence: Having a positive personality can help you deal with stress more effectively.
examples.trans: 拥有积极的性格可以帮助你更有效地应对压力。

examples.sentence: What attracts me most is not her appearance but her warm and generous personality.
examples.trans: 最吸引我的不是她的外表，而是她温暖大方的性格。

examples.sentence: A person's personality, shaped by both genetics and environment, plays a decisive role in career success.
examples.trans: 一个人的性格由基因和环境共同塑造，在职业成功中起着决定性作用。

flaws.usageZh: 可数名词，常指性格或事物上的小缺点、不完美之处。常见搭配：character flaws（性格缺陷）、minor flaws（小瑕疵）、flaws in the design（设计中的缺陷）。

examples.sentence: This cup has a small flaw, so it is cheaper.
examples.trans: 这个杯子有个小瑕疵，所以便宜一些。

examples.sentence: Nobody is perfect; we all have our own flaws.
examples.trans: 没有人是完美的，我们都有自己的缺点。

examples.sentence: The teacher pointed out several flaws in my essay and asked me to revise it.
examples.trans: 老师指出了我作文中的几处缺点，让我修改。

examples.sentence: Learning to accept your flaws is an important step toward building self-confidence.
examples.trans: 学会接受自己的缺点是建立自信的重要一步。

examples.sentence: Despite its minor flaws, the novel remains one of the most influential works of the century.
examples.trans: 尽管有细微的瑕疵，这部小说仍然是本世纪最具影响力的作品之一。

examples.sentence: The investigation revealed serious flaws in the safety system that had been overlooked for years.
examples.trans: 调查揭示了安全系统中多年来被忽视的严重缺陷。

prepared.usageZh: 形容词，常与 be、feel、get 等连用。常见搭配：be prepared for sth（为某事做好准备）、be prepared to do sth（愿意做某事/准备好做某事）、well prepared（准备充分的）。

examples.sentence: I am prepared for the school trip tomorrow.
examples.trans: 我为明天的学校旅行做好了准备。

examples.sentence: She got up early and prepared a big breakfast for the family.
examples.trans: 她起得很早，为家人准备了一顿丰盛的早餐。

examples.sentence: If you are well prepared before the exam, you will feel much less nervous.
examples.trans: 如果你考前准备充分，就会感觉不那么紧张。

examples.sentence: Having prepared all the necessary documents in advance, she walked into the interview with confidence.
examples.trans: 提前准备好了所有必要文件后，她自信地走进了面试室。

examples.sentence: The rescue team was fully prepared for the worst-case scenario, yet hoped for the best.
examples.trans: 救援队为最坏的情况做好了充分准备，但仍希望出现最好的结果。

examples.sentence: Students who are academically prepared and emotionally resilient tend to adapt more smoothly to university life.
examples.trans: 在学业上准备充分且情绪韧性强的大学生往往能更顺利地适应大学生活。

weaknesses.usageZh: 可数名词，是 weakness 的复数形式，表示“弱点、缺点”。常与 strengths 对比使用，常见搭配有 strengths and weaknesses（优点和缺点）、overcome one's weaknesses（克服弱点）。

examples.sentence: My biggest weakness is that I eat too much chocolate.
examples.trans: 我最大的缺点是吃太多巧克力。

examples.sentence: Everyone has weaknesses, so don't be afraid to ask for help.
examples.trans: 每个人都有弱点，所以不要害怕寻求帮助。

examples.sentence: She knows her weaknesses in math, so she practices extra problems every weekend.
examples.trans: 她知道自己在数学上的弱点，所以每个周末都额外练习题目。

examples.sentence: A good leader understands both the strengths and weaknesses of each team member.
examples.trans: 一个好的领导者了解每个团队成员的长处和短处。

examples.sentence: Rather than hiding his weaknesses, he chose to face them directly and work on them one by one.
examples.trans: 他没有隐藏自己的弱点，而是选择直接面对并逐一改进。

examples.sentence: The report identifies several weaknesses in the current system that must be addressed before the project can move forward.
examples.trans: 该报告指出了当前系统中必须解决的几个弱点，项目才能继续推进。

analyze.usageZh: 及物动词，后接名词或名词短语作宾语，表示“分析”。常见搭配有 analyze data（分析数据）、analyze a problem（分析问题）、analyze the results（分析结果）。

examples.sentence: We need to analyze the water to see if it is clean.
examples.trans: 我们需要分析一下水，看看它是否干净。

examples.sentence: The teacher asked us to analyze the main character's feelings in the story.
examples.trans: 老师让我们分析故事中主角的感受。

examples.sentence: Before making a decision, you should analyze all the possible choices carefully.
examples.trans: 在做决定之前，你应该仔细分析所有可能的选择。

examples.sentence: Researchers spent months analyzing the survey responses to identify patterns in consumer behavior.
examples.trans: 研究人员花了数月时间分析调查问卷，以找出消费者行为的规律。

examples.sentence: To fully understand the poem, one must analyze not only its language but also the historical context in which it was written.
examples.trans: 要完全理解这首诗，不仅要分析其语言，还要分析它创作时的历史背景。

examples.sentence: Economists analyzing the latest employment figures argue that the apparent growth masks deeper structural problems in the labor market.
examples.trans: 分析最新就业数据的经济学家认为，表面的增长掩盖了劳动力市场更深层的结构性问题。

confident.usageZh: 形容词，表示“自信的”。常作表语，与 be、feel、look、seem 等连用，也可作定语修饰名词。常见搭配有 be confident about/in（对……有信心）、feel confident（感到自信）。

examples.sentence: She feels confident when she sings in front of her family.
examples.trans: 她在家人面前唱歌时感到很自信。

examples.sentence: After practicing for two weeks, he became more confident about giving the speech.
examples.trans: 练习了两周后，他对做演讲更有信心了。

examples.sentence: If you review your notes every day, you will feel confident before the final exam.
examples.trans: 如果你每天复习笔记，期末考试前你就会感到自信。

examples.sentence: Having overcome several difficult challenges, she now feels confident enough to lead the project on her own.
examples.trans: 克服了几个困难的挑战后，她现在有足够的信心独自领导这个项目。

examples.sentence: He appeared calm and confident during the interview, yet his hands were trembling slightly under the table.
examples.trans: 面试时他显得冷静而自信，然而桌子底下的手却在微微颤抖。

examples.sentence: A confident speaker does not simply memorize lines but adapts naturally to the reactions of the audience.
examples.trans: 一个自信的演讲者不会只是背台词，而是能自然地根据听众的反应进行调整。

impression.usageZh: 可数名词，常与动词 make, leave, give 搭配，表示“留下印象”。常用形容词有 good, great, first, deep, lasting 等。口语和书面语都常见，first impression 是高频搭配。

family.meaning: 给……留下深刻印象；使钦佩
令人印象深刻的；令人赞叹的

examples.sentence: My first impression of the new school was very good.
examples.trans: 我对新学校的第一印象非常好。

examples.sentence: The clean classroom left a good impression on the visitors.
examples.trans: 干净的教室给来访者留下了好印象。

examples.sentence: Although he was nervous, he still made a strong impression in the interview.
examples.trans: 尽管他很紧张，他还是在面试中给人留下了深刻的印象。

examples.sentence: Having read her application carefully, I got the impression that she was genuinely interested in environmental science.
examples.trans: 仔细读完她的申请后，我的印象是她对环境科学真正感兴趣。

examples.sentence: What struck me most was not his academic record but the lasting impression of quiet confidence he conveyed.
examples.trans: 最打动我的不是他的学业成绩，而是他所传递出的那种沉静自信给人的持久印象。

examples.sentence: The survey reveals that consumers' first impression of a brand is formed within seconds, yet it may take years to reverse if negative.
examples.trans: 调查显示，消费者对品牌的第一印象在几秒钟内就会形成，但如果是负面的，可能需要数年才能扭转。

candidate.usageZh: 可数名词，指求职者、考生或选举候选人。常与 for 搭配，如 a candidate for the job。也可作定语，如 candidate list, candidate interview。正式程度中等，招聘和选举语境最常见。

family.meaning: 候选资格；候选人身份（英式）

examples.sentence: There are three candidates for the class monitor job.
examples.trans: 有三个候选人竞选班长这个职位。

examples.sentence: Each candidate needs to fill in a form before the interview.
examples.trans: 每位候选人面试前都需要填一张表格。

examples.sentence: The company will contact successful candidates by email within two weeks.
examples.trans: 公司将在两周内通过电子邮件联系成功入选的候选人。

examples.sentence: Candidates who fail to submit the required documents by Friday will not be considered for the position.
examples.trans: 未能在周五前提交所需文件的候选人将不被考虑该职位。

examples.sentence: Rather than focusing on a candidate's academic background alone, the panel placed equal weight on practical problem-solving ability.
examples.trans: 评审小组并没有只关注候选人的学术背景，而是同样重视实际解决问题的能力。

examples.sentence: Given the complexity of the role, the ideal candidate would combine technical expertise with the interpersonal skills required to lead a cross-functional team.
examples.trans: 考虑到该职位的复杂性，理想的候选人应兼具技术专长和领导跨职能团队所需的人际交往能力。

strengths.usageZh: 可数名词，strength 的复数形式，指个人或事物的优势、长处。常与 weaknesses 对比使用，如 strengths and weaknesses。也可与动词 build on, identify, recognize 搭配。

examples.sentence: My strengths are drawing and playing basketball.
examples.trans: 我的强项是画画和打篮球。

examples.sentence: The teacher asked us to write down our strengths and weaknesses.
examples.trans: 老师让我们写下自己的优点和缺点。

examples.sentence: If you know your strengths, you can use them to help your team win.
examples.trans: 如果你了解自己的优势，就可以利用它们帮助团队获胜。

examples.sentence: One of the greatest strengths of this research is that it draws on data collected over a ten-year period.
examples.trans: 这项研究最大的优势之一在于它利用了跨越十年收集的数据。

examples.sentence: While the proposal has obvious strengths in terms of cost efficiency, its long-term environmental impact remains open to question.
examples.trans: 尽管该方案在成本效益方面有明显优势，但其长期环境影响仍有待商榷。

examples.sentence: Effective leaders are those who not only recognize their own strengths but also build teams that compensate for their limitations.
examples.trans: 高效的领导者不仅认识到自己的优势，还能组建团队来弥补自身的不足。

appropriate.usageZh: 形容词，意为“合适的，恰当的”。常作定语或表语，如 an appropriate gift（一份合适的礼物）。常用搭配：be appropriate for/to（对……合适），it is appropriate to do sth（做某事是恰当的）。语体偏正式，口语和书面语均可使用。

examples.sentence: Shorts are not appropriate for a cold winter day.
examples.trans: 短裤在寒冷的冬天不合适。

examples.sentence: We need to choose an appropriate song for the school party.
examples.trans: 我们需要为学校聚会选一首合适的歌。

examples.sentence: It is appropriate to turn off your phone when you are in the library.
examples.trans: 在图书馆时关掉手机是合适的。

examples.sentence: The teacher asked us to use language appropriate to a formal presentation.
examples.trans: 老师要求我们使用适合正式展示的语言。

examples.sentence: Wearing a suit to a beach party would hardly be considered appropriate, no matter how expensive it is.
examples.trans: 无论西装多贵，穿着它去海滩聚会都很难被认为是合适的。

examples.sentence: Before making any public statement, the committee carefully considered whether the timing was appropriate given the sensitive nature of the issue.
examples.trans: 在发表任何公开声明之前，委员会仔细考虑了鉴于该问题的敏感性，时机是否恰当。

exaggerating.usageZh: 形容词，意为“夸张的，言过其实的”。是动词 exaggerate 的现在分词形式，常作定语修饰名词，如 an exaggerating tone（夸张的语气）。口语中也可说 You're exaggerating（你太夸张了），此时为动词进行时。作形容词时语体偏口语化。

examples.sentence: My little brother has an exaggerating way of saying he is hungry.
examples.trans: 我弟弟说他饿的时候总是很夸张。

examples.sentence: She told an exaggerating story about a fish that was as big as a car.
examples.trans: 她讲了一个夸张的故事，说一条鱼有汽车那么大。

examples.sentence: His exaggerating description of the trip made everyone laugh, even though we knew it wasn't all true.
examples.trans: 他对这次旅行夸张的描述让大家都笑了，尽管我们知道并不全是真的。

examples.sentence: The advertisement used an exaggerating claim that the drink could make you run faster overnight.
examples.trans: 这则广告使用了一个夸张的说法，声称这种饮料能让你一夜之间跑得更快。

examples.sentence: Critics pointed out that the documentary's exaggerating tone weakened its credibility, despite the real issues it raised.
examples.trans: 评论家指出，这部纪录片夸张的语气削弱了它的可信度，尽管它提出了真实的问题。

examples.sentence: An exaggerating account of a minor incident can sometimes cause more damage than the incident itself, especially when it spreads rapidly online.
examples.trans: 对一个小事件的夸张描述有时比事件本身造成的损害更大，尤其是当它在网上迅速传播时。

professional.usageZh: 形容词，意为“职业的，专业的”。可作定语或表语，如 professional training（专业训练）、a professional athlete（职业运动员）。也可作名词，意为“专业人士”。常用搭配：professional advice（专业建议）、professional attitude（专业态度）。语体中性，口语和书面语均常用。

examples.sentence: My uncle is a professional basketball player.
examples.trans: 我叔叔是一名职业篮球运动员。

examples.sentence: The doctor gave us professional advice about how to stay healthy.
examples.trans: 医生就如何保持健康给了我们专业的建议。

examples.sentence: If you want to fix the computer safely, you should ask a professional for help.
examples.trans: 如果你想安全地修好电脑，你应该向专业人士求助。

examples.sentence: Having a professional attitude means taking responsibility for your work and treating others with respect.
examples.trans: 拥有专业的态度意味着对自己的工作负责并尊重他人。

examples.sentence: Although she is still a student, her presentation was so well-structured and polished that it felt entirely professional.
examples.trans: 尽管她还是一名学生，但她的展示结构清晰、打磨精良，感觉完全是专业水准。

examples.sentence: The company's reputation for professional integrity has allowed it to attract top talent even in a highly competitive market.
examples.trans: 该公司在职业操守方面的声誉使其即使在竞争激烈的市场中也能吸引顶尖人才。

decent.usageZh: 形容词，可作定语或表语。表示“体面的、得体的”或“相当好的、不错的”。口语中常用来表示某物质量或数量令人满意，如 a decent meal, a decent salary。描述行为时表示合乎道德或社会规范。

family.meaning: 体面地；得体地；相当好地

examples.sentence: My mom bought me a decent backpack for school.
examples.trans: 妈妈给我买了一个相当不错的书包。

examples.sentence: The hotel was small but the room was clean and decent.
examples.trans: 那家旅馆很小，但房间干净而且挺不错。

examples.sentence: He earns a decent salary, so he can afford to travel once a year.
examples.trans: 他挣的工资相当不错，所以能负担得起一年旅行一次。

examples.sentence: After weeks of training, she finally ran a decent time in the 800 meters.
examples.trans: 经过几周的训练，她终于在800米比赛中跑出了一个相当好的成绩。

examples.sentence: It is only decent to thank the people who helped you along the way.
examples.trans: 感谢一路上帮助过你的人，这是起码的礼貌。

examples.sentence: Given the limited budget, the committee managed to produce a decent report that addressed the key issues.
examples.trans: 考虑到预算有限，委员会还是设法完成了一份相当不错的报告，涵盖了关键问题。

positive.usageZh: 形容词，可作定语或表语。表示“积极的、乐观的”或“正面的、肯定的”。常见搭配有 positive attitude, positive effect, positive response。反义词为 negative。

examples.sentence: Try to think positive thoughts before the exam.
examples.trans: 考试前尽量想一些积极的想法。

examples.sentence: The teacher gave me positive feedback on my science project.
examples.trans: 老师对我的科学项目给出了正面的反馈。

examples.sentence: Regular exercise has a positive effect on both your body and your mood.
examples.trans: 经常锻炼对身体和情绪都有积极的影响。

examples.sentence: Having a positive role model can shape a teenager's values in lasting ways.
examples.trans: 拥有一个积极的榜样能以持久的方式塑造青少年的价值观。

examples.sentence: The new policy received a largely positive response from local businesses, though a few remained skeptical.
examples.trans: 新政策得到了当地企业大体上正面的回应，尽管少数企业仍持怀疑态度。

examples.sentence: Maintaining a positive outlook does not mean ignoring problems, but rather approaching them with the belief that solutions exist.
examples.trans: 保持积极的心态并不意味着忽视问题，而是以相信解决方案存在的态度去面对它们。

majority.usageZh: 名词，常与 the 连用，表示“大多数、大部分”。常见结构为 the majority of + 复数名词/不可数名词。作主语时，谓语动词的单复数取决于 of 后面的名词。也可单独使用，如 in the majority（占多数）。

examples.sentence: The majority of my friends like playing video games.
examples.trans: 我的大多数朋友喜欢玩电子游戏。

examples.sentence: The majority of the students in our class walk to school.
examples.trans: 我们班大多数学生步行上学。

examples.sentence: The majority of the information on the website is available in both Chinese and English.
examples.trans: 该网站上的大部分信息都有中英文两种版本。

examples.sentence: Although a few members disagreed, the majority voted in favor of the new schedule.
examples.trans: 尽管少数成员不同意，大多数人投票赞成新的时间安排。

examples.sentence: The vast majority of respondents indicated that they would support stricter environmental regulations.
examples.trans: 绝大多数受访者表示他们会支持更严格的环境法规。

examples.sentence: While the majority of the evidence supports the theory, a small but significant portion remains difficult to explain.
examples.trans: 虽然大多数证据支持这一理论，但仍有一小部分重要内容难以解释。

mock.usageZh: 形容词，常作定语修饰名词，如 mock exam（模拟考试）、mock interview（模拟面试）、mock trial（模拟法庭）。也可作动词，表示“嘲笑”或“模仿”。语体偏正式，常见于教育、职场场景。

examples.sentence: We had a mock exam in class today, but it was not the real one.
examples.trans: 我们今天在课堂上做了一次模拟考试，但不是真的考试。

examples.sentence: The students took a mock interview to practice answering questions before the real one.
examples.trans: 学生们在真正的面试之前进行了一次模拟面试来练习回答问题。

examples.sentence: The school arranged a mock trial so that students could understand how a court works.
examples.trans: 学校安排了一场模拟法庭，让学生了解法庭是如何运作的。

examples.sentence: Having completed several mock tests under timed conditions, she felt far more confident about the actual exam.
examples.trans: 在限时条件下完成了几次模拟测试后，她对真正的考试感到自信多了。

examples.sentence: The mock negotiation exercise revealed that many participants struggled to respond calmly under pressure.
examples.trans: 这场模拟谈判练习暴露出许多参与者在压力下难以冷静应对。

examples.sentence: Although the mock data set was artificially generated, it closely mirrored the patterns found in real-world clinical trials.
examples.trans: 尽管这组模拟数据是人工生成的，但它高度还原了真实世界临床试验中发现的模式。

common.usageZh: 形容词，表示“常见的、普遍的、共同的”。可作定语或表语。常用句型：It is common for sb to do sth（某人做某事很常见）；have sth in common（有共同之处）。口语和书面语都常用。

examples.sentence: Tom and I have a common hobby: we both like playing basketball.
examples.trans: 汤姆和我有一个共同的爱好：我们都喜欢打篮球。

examples.sentence: It is common for young children to feel nervous on their first day at a new school.
examples.trans: 小孩子在新学校的第一天感到紧张是很常见的。

examples.sentence: Colds are common in winter, so doctors advise people to wash their hands often.
examples.trans: 感冒在冬天很常见，所以医生建议人们勤洗手。

examples.sentence: What these two theories have in common is that both emphasize the role of early experience in shaping personality.
examples.trans: 这两种理论的共同之处在于，都强调早期经历在塑造人格中的作用。

examples.sentence: Contrary to common belief, the study found no direct link between screen time and declining eyesight among teenagers.
examples.trans: 与普遍看法相反，这项研究发现青少年使用屏幕的时间与视力下降之间没有直接联系。

examples.sentence: A common thread running through these seemingly unrelated cases is the failure to account for long-term environmental costs.
examples.trans: 贯穿这些看似无关案例的一条共同主线是，都未能将长期环境成本纳入考量。

actively.usageZh: 副词，修饰动词，表示“积极地、主动地”。常见搭配：actively participate（积极参与）、actively seek（积极寻求）、actively encourage（积极鼓励）。多用于正式或半正式语境。

examples.sentence: My sister actively helps my mom clean the house every weekend.
examples.trans: 我姐姐每个周末都主动帮妈妈打扫房子。

examples.sentence: The teacher asked us to actively take part in the school sports meeting.
examples.trans: 老师要求我们积极参加学校运动会。

examples.sentence: If you actively listen to others, you will understand their feelings much better.
examples.trans: 如果你积极地倾听别人，你会更好地理解他们的感受。

examples.sentence: Students who actively engage with the material, rather than simply memorizing it, tend to retain knowledge far longer.
examples.trans: 主动钻研材料而不是单纯死记硬背的学生，往往能更长久地记住知识。

examples.sentence: The company has been actively pursuing partnerships with local universities to accelerate research on renewable energy.
examples.trans: 该公司一直在积极寻求与当地大学建立合作关系，以加速可再生能源的研究。

examples.sentence: Governments must actively intervene in housing markets when speculation begins to price out essential workers from urban centers.
examples.trans: 当投机行为开始把核心劳动者挤出城市中心时，政府必须积极干预住房市场。

immune.usageZh: 形容词 (adjective)。常与 'system' 连用为 'immune system'（免疫系统），也可接 'to' 表示“不受……影响”。可用于医学语境，也可引申为“对批评、压力等无动于衷”。

examples.sentence: A baby gets immune protection from its mother's milk.
examples.trans: 婴儿从母乳中获得免疫保护。

examples.sentence: Washing your hands often helps your immune system stay strong.
examples.trans: 经常洗手有助于保持免疫系统强健。

examples.sentence: Once you have had chickenpox, you are usually immune to it for life.
examples.trans: 一旦得过水痘，通常就会终身免疫。

examples.sentence: Lack of sleep can weaken the immune system, making people more likely to catch colds.
examples.trans: 睡眠不足会削弱免疫系统，使人更容易感冒。

examples.sentence: No one is immune to criticism, but confident people tend to handle it more calmly.
examples.trans: 没有人对批评完全免疫，但自信的人往往能更冷静地应对。

examples.sentence: Chronic stress has been shown to suppress immune function, leaving the body vulnerable to infection.
examples.trans: 慢性压力已被证明会抑制免疫功能，使身体容易受到感染。

cardiovascular.usageZh: 形容词 (adjective)。医学及健康领域常用词，指与心脏和血管相关的。常搭配 'system'（系统）、'disease'（疾病）、'exercise'（运动）、'health'（健康）。

examples.sentence: Swimming is good for your cardiovascular health.
examples.trans: 游泳对心血管健康有好处。

examples.sentence: Doctors say walking every day can lower the risk of cardiovascular problems.
examples.trans: 医生说每天走路可以降低心血管问题的风险。

examples.sentence: Eating too much salt may lead to high blood pressure and other cardiovascular diseases.
examples.trans: 吃太多盐可能导致高血压和其他心血管疾病。

examples.sentence: Regular aerobic training improves cardiovascular endurance, allowing the heart to pump blood more efficiently.
examples.trans: 规律的有氧训练能提高心血管耐力，使心脏更高效地泵血。

examples.sentence: While genetics play a role, lifestyle choices such as diet and exercise heavily influence cardiovascular outcomes.
examples.trans: 虽然基因有一定作用，但饮食和运动等生活方式选择对心血管健康结果影响很大。

examples.sentence: Epidemiological studies consistently link prolonged sitting with elevated cardiovascular mortality, independent of exercise habits.
examples.trans: 流行病学研究一致表明，久坐与心血管死亡率升高相关，且这一关联不受运动习惯影响。

lonely.usageZh: 形容词 (adjective)。描述因缺少陪伴而产生的悲伤情绪。注意与 'alone'（独自一人，客观状态）区分：'lonely' 是主观感受。常作表语，如 'feel lonely'。

examples.sentence: The little dog looked lonely in the empty house.
examples.trans: 小狗在空荡荡的房子里看起来很孤独。

examples.sentence: He felt lonely on his first day at the new school because he knew no one.
examples.trans: 在新学校的第一天他感到孤独，因为他谁也不认识。

examples.sentence: Although she lives alone, she rarely feels lonely because she has many good friends nearby.
examples.trans: 虽然她一个人住，但她很少感到孤独，因为附近有很多好朋友。

examples.sentence: Moving to a big city can be exciting, yet many young people find themselves feeling unexpectedly lonely.
examples.trans: 搬到大城市可能令人兴奋，但许多年轻人却发现自己出乎意料地感到孤独。

examples.sentence: Surrounded by crowds but disconnected from meaningful relationships, a person can feel lonelier than someone living in isolation.
examples.trans: 被人群包围却缺乏有意义的关系，一个人可能比独居者更感孤独。

examples.sentence: Research suggests that chronic loneliness triggers the same neural pathways as physical pain, underscoring the deep human need for social connection.
examples.trans: 研究表明，长期孤独会激活与身体疼痛相同的神经通路，凸显了人类对社交联系的深层需求。

crucial.usageZh: 形容词，表示“至关重要的、决定性的”。常作表语：be crucial for/to sb/sth；也可作定语：a crucial moment/decision。比 important 语气更强，多用于强调某事物不可或缺或影响成败。

examples.sentence: Breakfast is crucial before a long school day.
examples.trans: 在上学一整天之前，吃早餐很关键。

examples.sentence: The goalkeeper made a crucial save in the last minute of the match.
examples.trans: 守门员在比赛最后一分钟做出了一次关键的扑救。

examples.sentence: Getting enough sleep is crucial if you want to stay focused during exams.
examples.trans: 如果你想在考试期间保持专注，充足的睡眠至关重要。

examples.sentence: Understanding the target audience is crucial to designing an effective advertising campaign.
examples.trans: 了解目标受众对设计有效的广告活动至关重要。

examples.sentence: What proved crucial was not the amount of funding but the team's ability to adapt quickly.
examples.trans: 最终被证明至关重要的不是资金数量，而是团队快速适应的能力。

examples.sentence: The ability to distinguish reliable sources from misinformation has become crucial in an era dominated by social media.
examples.trans: 在社交媒体主导的时代，区分可靠信息与错误信息的能力已变得至关重要。

interaction.usageZh: 名词，表示“互动、交流、相互作用”。常见搭配：social interaction（社交互动）、human-computer interaction（人机交互）、interaction between A and B。可指人与人、人与物或物与物之间的相互影响。

examples.sentence: My little brother enjoys interaction with his classmates at lunchtime.
examples.trans: 我弟弟喜欢午餐时和同学们互动。

examples.sentence: Group games encourage interaction among children who do not know each other well.
examples.trans: 小组游戏能鼓励不太熟悉的孩子之间进行互动。

examples.sentence: Regular interaction with native speakers is one of the fastest ways to improve your spoken English.
examples.trans: 经常与母语者交流是提高英语口语最快的方法之一。

examples.sentence: The study examines how online interaction affects teenagers' sense of belonging.
examples.trans: 这项研究考察了线上互动如何影响青少年的归属感。

examples.sentence: Face-to-face interaction, unlike text messaging, allows people to pick up on tone and body language.
examples.trans: 与发短信不同，面对面的互动能让人们捕捉到语气和肢体语言。

examples.sentence: Researchers argue that meaningful social interaction, rather than passive consumption of content, is what sustains long-term user engagement on digital platforms.
examples.trans: 研究人员认为，维持数字平台长期用户参与度的是有意义的社交互动，而非被动消费内容。

hormone.usageZh: 名词，指“激素、荷尔蒙”。常见搭配：growth hormone（生长激素）、stress hormone（压力激素）、hormone levels（激素水平）。多用于生物、医学及描述情绪或身体变化的语境。

family.meaning: 在激素方面；由激素引起地

examples.sentence: A special hormone helps your body grow taller when you are young.
examples.trans: 你小时候有一种特殊的激素帮助身体长高。

examples.sentence: When you feel scared, your body releases a hormone that makes your heart beat faster.
examples.trans: 当你感到害怕时，身体会释放一种让心跳加快的激素。

examples.sentence: Doctors checked whether his hormone levels were normal after he felt tired for weeks.
examples.trans: 在他连续几周感到疲倦后，医生检查了他的激素水平是否正常。

examples.sentence: Lack of sunlight can affect the production of a hormone that regulates sleep.
examples.trans: 缺乏阳光会影响一种调节睡眠的激素的分泌。

examples.sentence: The hormone cortisol, often called the stress hormone, rises sharply when a person faces a tight deadline.
examples.trans: 皮质醇这种激素通常被称为压力激素，当人面对紧迫的截止日期时会急剧上升。

examples.sentence: Chronic sleep deprivation disrupts the balance of hormones that control appetite, which may explain why exhausted individuals often crave high-calorie food.
examples.trans: 长期睡眠不足会扰乱控制食欲的激素平衡，这或许能解释为什么极度疲惫的人常常渴望高热量食物。

appreciated.usageZh: 形容词，常作表语，用于 be appreciated 结构，表示“被感激、被重视”。主语可以是人，也可以是帮助、努力、建议等抽象名词。口语和书面语都常用，语气比 thanked 更正式一些。

family.meaning: 表示感激的；有欣赏力的

examples.sentence: Your help is much appreciated.
examples.trans: 非常感谢你的帮助。

examples.sentence: The teacher said our hard work was appreciated by the whole school.
examples.trans: 老师说我们的努力得到了全校的认可。

examples.sentence: Small acts of kindness are often appreciated more than expensive gifts.
examples.trans: 小小的善举往往比昂贵的礼物更让人感激。

examples.sentence: Having my suggestions appreciated by the team gave me the confidence to speak up more often.
examples.trans: 我的建议得到团队的认可，这给了我更多发言的信心。

examples.sentence: While her efforts went largely unnoticed at the time, they were deeply appreciated in retrospect.
examples.trans: 虽然她的努力当时大多未被注意，但事后回想起来却深受感激。

examples.sentence: The subtle irony in the novel is only fully appreciated by readers familiar with the historical context.
examples.trans: 小说中微妙的讽刺只有熟悉历史背景的读者才能充分领会。

socialize.usageZh: 动词，不及物，常与 with 连用，表示“与某人交往、社交”。也可作及物动词，表示“使社会化”。日常口语和书面语都常见，强调轻松、非正式的互动。

examples.sentence: My dog loves to socialize with other dogs at the park.
examples.trans: 我的狗喜欢在公园里和其他狗一起玩。

examples.sentence: After moving to a new city, she found it hard to socialize with her classmates at first.
examples.trans: 搬到新城市后，她一开始觉得很难和同学交往。

examples.sentence: Joining a club is a great way to socialize with people who share your interests.
examples.trans: 加入社团是和志趣相投的人交往的好方法。

examples.sentence: Remote workers often need to make a conscious effort to socialize, as casual office interactions are absent.
examples.trans: 远程工作者往往需要有意识地去社交，因为办公室里随意的互动不存在了。

examples.sentence: Unlike his brother, who thrives in large gatherings, Tom prefers to socialize in small, familiar groups.
examples.trans: 与他喜欢大型聚会的哥哥不同，汤姆更喜欢在小而熟悉的圈子里社交。

examples.sentence: The study suggests that elderly people who socialize regularly tend to maintain sharper cognitive function than those who remain isolated.
examples.trans: 研究表明，经常社交的老年人往往比独处的老年人保持更敏锐的认知功能。

connection.usageZh: 名词，可数或不可数。常指人与人之间的“联系、关系”，也可指事物之间的“关联”或网络、交通等的“连接”。常见搭配：make a connection, have a connection with, a strong/close connection, internet connection。

examples.sentence: There is a strong connection between my phone and the Wi-Fi at home.
examples.trans: 我的手机和家里的无线网络连接很强。

examples.sentence: She felt an instant connection with her new pen pal from Japan.
examples.trans: 她和来自日本的新笔友立刻有了一种亲近感。

examples.sentence: Scientists have found a clear connection between regular exercise and better sleep.
examples.trans: 科学家发现经常锻炼和更好的睡眠之间有明显的联系。

examples.sentence: Having a personal connection to the cause made her fundraising efforts far more passionate.
examples.trans: 与这项事业有个人渊源使她的筹款工作更加充满热情。

examples.sentence: The connection between early childhood experiences and adult behavior has been widely documented in psychological research.
examples.trans: 童年早期经历与成年行为之间的联系已在心理学研究中得到广泛证实。

examples.sentence: Despite living in an era of unprecedented digital connection, many people report feeling more isolated than ever before.
examples.trans: 尽管生活在一个数字连接空前发达的时代，许多人却表示比以往任何时候都更感到孤独。

tragedy.usageZh: 名词 (noun)。可数名词，指非常悲伤或灾难性的事件。常见搭配：a terrible tragedy, end in tragedy, prevent a tragedy。可用于描述个人不幸或公共灾难。

examples.sentence: The fire was a tragedy, but no one was hurt.
examples.trans: 那场火灾是一场灾难，但没有人受伤。

examples.sentence: Losing the final match felt like a tragedy to the young players.
examples.trans: 输掉决赛对这些年轻球员来说就像一场悲剧。

examples.sentence: The whole city was shocked when the tragedy happened on the bridge.
examples.trans: 当悲剧在桥上发生时，整座城市都震惊了。

examples.sentence: It would be a tragedy if the old library were torn down to build a parking lot.
examples.trans: 如果旧图书馆被拆掉来建停车场，那将是一场悲剧。

examples.sentence: The play begins as a comedy but gradually turns into a tragedy in the final act.
examples.trans: 这部剧以喜剧开场，但在最后一幕逐渐转变为悲剧。

examples.sentence: What makes the tragedy even more painful is that it could have been prevented with proper safety checks.
examples.trans: 让这场悲剧更加令人痛心的是，如果进行了适当的安全检查，它本可以避免。

negative.usageZh: 形容词 (adjective)。与 positive 相对，用于描述态度、影响、情绪、结果等。常见搭配：negative effect, negative attitude, negative result, in a negative way。

examples.sentence: Don't say negative things about your friends.
examples.trans: 不要说朋友的坏话。

examples.sentence: Too much screen time can have a negative effect on your sleep.
examples.trans: 看屏幕时间太长会对你的睡眠产生负面影响。

examples.sentence: She stayed calm even when she received negative feedback on her project.
examples.trans: 即使她的项目收到了负面反馈，她仍然保持冷静。

examples.sentence: Constant criticism creates a negative atmosphere that discourages people from trying new ideas.
examples.trans: 不断的批评会营造一种消极的氛围，使人们不敢尝试新想法。

examples.sentence: While the report highlights some negative trends, it also points to several encouraging signs of recovery.
examples.trans: 虽然报告强调了一些负面趋势，但它也指出了几个令人鼓舞的复苏迹象。

examples.sentence: The negative consequences of ignoring early warning signs often far outweigh the short-term costs of taking preventive action.
examples.trans: 忽视早期预警信号所带来的负面后果，往往远远超过采取预防措施的短期成本。

audience.usageZh: 名词 (noun)。集合名词，通常用单数形式，指观看或聆听的一群人。常见搭配：a large audience, target audience, live audience, audience member。谓语动词可用单数或复数，视语境而定。

examples.sentence: The audience clapped loudly after the song.
examples.trans: 歌曲结束后，观众大声鼓掌。

examples.sentence: The magician asked for a volunteer from the audience to come on stage.
examples.trans: 魔术师请一位观众上台做志愿者。

examples.sentence: The audience was so moved by the speech that many people stood up to applaud.
examples.trans: 观众被演讲深深打动，许多人站起来鼓掌。

examples.sentence: Understanding your target audience is the first step in designing an effective advertising campaign.
examples.trans: 了解你的目标受众是设计有效广告活动的第一步。

examples.sentence: Unlike a film audience, a theatre audience can directly influence the energy of a live performance.
examples.trans: 与电影观众不同，剧场观众可以直接影响现场演出的能量。

examples.sentence: A skilled presenter reads the audience's body language and adjusts the pace of the talk accordingly.
examples.trans: 熟练的演讲者会观察观众的肢体语言，并相应地调整演讲节奏。

linger.usageZh: 动词 (verb)。不及物动词，常指不愉快的感觉、气味或记忆持续存在，常用 'linger on'。也可指人在某处逗留过久。

examples.sentence: Don't linger outside the school gate after class.
examples.trans: 放学后不要在校门口逗留。

examples.sentence: The taste of the chocolate lingered in my mouth for a long time.
examples.trans: 巧克力的味道在我嘴里久久不散。

examples.sentence: Although the meeting was over, a few people lingered to ask questions.
examples.trans: 虽然会议结束了，仍有几个人留下来问问题。

examples.sentence: Having said goodbye to her friends, she lingered at the station, unwilling to leave.
examples.trans: 和朋友们道别后，她在车站徘徊，不愿离去。

examples.sentence: The memory of that embarrassing moment lingered on, much longer than he had expected.
examples.trans: 那个尴尬时刻的记忆久久不散，比他预想的长得多。

examples.sentence: Concerns about the long-term effects of the policy linger among economists, despite the government's reassurances.
examples.trans: 尽管政府作出了保证，经济学家们对该政策长期影响的担忧仍然存在。

compliment.usageZh: 名词 (noun)。可数名词，表示赞美或恭维。常用搭配：'pay someone a compliment'（赞美某人）、'take it as a compliment'（把它当作夸奖）。注意与 complement（补充）区分。

examples.sentence: My mom gave me a compliment on my new haircut.
examples.trans: 妈妈夸了我的新发型。

examples.sentence: He paid her a compliment on her beautiful handwriting.
examples.trans: 他夸她的字写得漂亮。

examples.sentence: She smiled and took his words as a compliment, even though she wasn't sure he meant it.
examples.trans: 她笑了笑，把他的话当作夸奖，尽管她不确定他是否是认真的。

examples.sentence: Receiving a sincere compliment from her strict teacher made her feel truly proud of her work.
examples.trans: 从严厉的老师那里得到真诚的赞美，让她对自己的作品感到由衷的自豪。

examples.sentence: Rather than fishing for compliments, she preferred to let her work speak for itself.
examples.trans: 与其刻意寻求赞美，她更愿意让作品本身说话。

examples.sentence: The critic's review was filled with backhanded compliments that praised the film's ambition while dismissing its execution.
examples.trans: 那位评论家的影评充满了明褒暗贬之词，既称赞影片的雄心，又否定其执行效果。

sincere.usageZh: 形容词 (adjective)。用于描述情感、兴趣、道歉、感谢等，表示发自内心的、不虚伪的。常用搭配：'sincere interest'、'sincere apology'、'sincere gratitude'。副词形式为 sincerely。

examples.sentence: Thank you for your sincere help with my homework.
examples.trans: 谢谢你真诚地帮我做作业。

examples.sentence: She showed a sincere interest in learning about different cultures.
examples.trans: 她对了解不同文化表现出真诚的兴趣。

examples.sentence: He offered a sincere apology after he realized he had hurt his friend's feelings.
examples.trans: 当他意识到自己伤害了朋友的感情后，他真诚地道了歉。

examples.sentence: To build trust with your teammates, you need to show sincere concern for their difficulties.
examples.trans: 要与队友建立信任，你需要真诚地关心他们的困难。

examples.sentence: Her sincere enthusiasm for the project was far more convincing than any polished presentation could have been.
examples.trans: 她对该项目发自内心的热情，比任何精心打磨的演示都更有说服力。

examples.sentence: A sincere willingness to acknowledge one's own mistakes is often regarded as a hallmark of genuine leadership.
examples.trans: 真诚地愿意承认自己的错误，往往被视为真正领导力的标志。

fatigue.usageZh: 名词（也可作动词），作名词时通常不可数，表示身体或精神上的极度疲劳。常见搭配：suffer from fatigue（感到疲劳）、mental/physical fatigue（精神/身体疲劳）、battle fatigue（对抗疲劳）。作动词时表示“使疲劳”，较正式。

examples.sentence: After the long run, I felt a lot of fatigue in my legs.
examples.trans: 长跑之后，我的腿感到非常疲劳。

examples.sentence: Drinking enough water can help you avoid fatigue on hot days.
examples.trans: 在炎热的天气里，喝足够的水可以帮助你避免疲劳。

examples.sentence: The doctor said her constant fatigue might be caused by staying up too late.
examples.trans: 医生说，她持续的疲劳可能是由熬夜太多引起的。

examples.sentence: Ignoring early signs of fatigue can lead to serious mistakes at work.
examples.trans: 忽视疲劳的早期信号可能会导致工作中的严重错误。

examples.sentence: Mental fatigue, unlike physical tiredness, does not always disappear after a good night's sleep.
examples.trans: 与身体上的疲倦不同，精神疲劳并不总能在好好睡一觉之后消失。

examples.sentence: Prolonged exposure to high-stress environments often results in chronic fatigue, which in turn weakens the immune system.
examples.trans: 长期处于高压环境中往往会导致慢性疲劳，进而削弱免疫系统。

achievement.usageZh: 可数名词，表示通过努力、勇气或技能取得的成就。常见搭配：a sense of achievement（成就感）、academic achievement（学业成绩）、celebrate an achievement（庆祝成就）、be proud of one's achievement（为某人的成就感到骄傲）。

examples.sentence: Learning to ride a bike was a big achievement for my little brother.
examples.trans: 学会骑自行车对我弟弟来说是一个很大的成就。

examples.sentence: She felt a strong sense of achievement after finishing the difficult puzzle.
examples.trans: 完成那个困难的拼图后，她感到一种强烈的成就感。

examples.sentence: The school held a ceremony to celebrate the students' achievements in sports and art.
examples.trans: 学校举行了一个仪式，庆祝学生们在体育和艺术方面取得的成就。

examples.sentence: Being selected for the national team was an achievement that required years of dedicated training.
examples.trans: 入选国家队是一项需要多年刻苦训练的成就。

examples.sentence: While academic achievement is important, the ability to work well with others is equally valued by employers.
examples.trans: 虽然学业成绩很重要，但与他人良好合作的能力同样受到雇主的重视。

examples.sentence: The breakthrough in renewable energy technology represents a remarkable achievement that could reshape global energy policies.
examples.trans: 可再生能源技术的突破代表了一项非凡的成就，可能重塑全球能源政策。

sorrow.usageZh: 名词，表示深切的悲伤，常作不可数名词。常见搭配：deep sorrow（深深的悲伤）、express sorrow（表达悲痛）、feel sorrow for（为……感到难过）、joys and sorrows（欢乐与悲伤）。复数形式 sorrows 可指多种令人悲伤的事。

examples.sentence: The little girl's eyes were full of sorrow when her cat ran away.
examples.trans: 当小猫跑掉时，小女孩的眼里充满了悲伤。

examples.sentence: He tried to hide his sorrow, but his voice sounded very sad.
examples.trans: 他试图掩饰悲伤，但他的声音听起来非常难过。

examples.sentence: The whole village shared the family's sorrow after the terrible accident.
examples.trans: 那场可怕的事故之后，全村人都分担着那个家庭的悲痛。

examples.sentence: She found it hard to express the deep sorrow she felt after losing her grandmother.
examples.trans: 失去祖母后，她发现自己很难表达内心深处的悲痛。

examples.sentence: Unlike anger, which often fades quickly, sorrow can linger quietly in the heart for years.
examples.trans: 与往往很快消退的愤怒不同，悲伤可以在心中静静地停留多年。

examples.sentence: The novel explores how individuals transform personal sorrow into creative energy that benefits the wider community.
examples.trans: 这部小说探讨了个人如何将自身的悲伤转化为惠及更广泛社区的创造力。

substitute.usageZh: 可作名词或动词。名词：替代品，常用搭配 'be a substitute for'。动词：代替，常用搭配 'substitute A for B'（用A代替B）。注意动词用法中 A 是替代品，B 是被替代的原物。

examples.sentence: My mom used apples as a substitute for eggs in the cake.
examples.trans: 我妈妈用苹果代替蛋糕里的鸡蛋。

examples.sentence: The coach sent a substitute onto the field in the second half.
examples.trans: 教练在下半场派了一名替补上场。

examples.sentence: If you don't have butter, you can substitute vegetable oil for it.
examples.trans: 如果你没有黄油，可以用植物油代替。

examples.sentence: Nothing can substitute for the experience of travelling in person.
examples.trans: 没有什么能代替亲身旅行的体验。

examples.sentence: While online courses are convenient, they are by no means a substitute for face-to-face interaction.
examples.trans: 虽然线上课程很方便，但它们绝不能替代面对面的互动。

examples.sentence: The committee concluded that reducing class sizes could not substitute for improving the quality of teaching itself.
examples.trans: 委员会得出结论：缩小班级规模不能替代提高教学质量本身。

isolated.usageZh: 形容词。描述地点：偏远的、与外界隔绝的；描述人：孤独的、被孤立的。常用搭配：'feel isolated'（感到孤立）、'become isolated'（变得孤立）、'an isolated village'（偏远的村庄）。

examples.sentence: The small house stands on an isolated hill far from the town.
examples.trans: 那座小房子坐落在远离城镇的偏僻小山上。

examples.sentence: After moving to the new city, she felt isolated because she had no friends there.
examples.trans: 搬到新城市后，她感到很孤独，因为在那里没有朋友。

examples.sentence: The village became completely isolated after the heavy snow blocked the only road.
examples.trans: 大雪封住了唯一的路后，这个村庄完全与外界隔绝了。

examples.sentence: Working from home for months made him feel increasingly isolated from his colleagues.
examples.trans: 在家工作了几个月，他感到与同事越来越疏远。

examples.sentence: The study found that elderly people living alone are more likely to feel socially isolated than those who live with family.
examples.trans: 研究发现，独居老人比与家人同住的老人更容易感到社交孤立。

examples.sentence: Rather than treating each error as an isolated incident, the report argues that these failures reflect a systemic problem within the organization.
examples.trans: 该报告认为，这些失误并非孤立事件，而是反映了组织内部的系统性问题。

to some extent.usageZh: 介词短语，用作状语，通常放在句首或句中，表示“在某种程度上、部分地”。常用于书面语和口语中，用来缓和语气或限定范围。

examples.sentence: To some extent, I like rainy days because I can stay home.
examples.trans: 在某种程度上，我喜欢下雨天，因为我可以待在家里。

examples.sentence: To some extent, doing homework helps us remember what we learned.
examples.trans: 在某种程度上，做作业帮助我们记住学过的东西。

examples.sentence: To some extent, a person's habits are shaped by the environment they grow up in.
examples.trans: 在某种程度上，一个人的习惯是由其成长环境塑造的。

examples.sentence: To some extent, the success of a team depends on how well its members communicate with one another.
examples.trans: 在某种程度上，一个团队的成功取决于成员之间沟通得有多好。

examples.sentence: To some extent, the decline in reading habits can be attributed to the rise of short-form video content.
examples.trans: 在某种程度上，阅读习惯的下降可以归因于短视频内容的兴起。

examples.sentence: To some extent, economic growth is driven by technological innovation, yet it also creates new social inequalities that demand attention.
examples.trans: 在某种程度上，经济增长由技术创新驱动，但它也带来了需要关注的新社会不平等。

benefit you.usageZh: 动词短语，benefit 为及物动词，后接人称代词或名词，表示“使……受益、对……有益”。常用于建议、说明利弊的语境中。

examples.sentence: Drinking more water every day will benefit you.
examples.trans: 每天多喝水会对你有好处。

examples.sentence: Learning to manage your time well will benefit you in many ways.
examples.trans: 学会管理时间会在很多方面对你有益。

examples.sentence: Taking regular exercise will benefit you not only physically but also mentally.
examples.trans: 经常锻炼不仅对身体有益，对心理也有好处。

examples.sentence: Developing the habit of reading critically will benefit you throughout your academic life.
examples.trans: 养成批判性阅读的习惯将使你在整个学术生涯中受益。

examples.sentence: While it may seem demanding at first, learning a second language will benefit you in ways you cannot yet imagine.
examples.trans: 虽然一开始可能看起来很吃力，但学习第二语言会以你尚无法想象的方式使你受益。

examples.sentence: Cultivating emotional resilience will benefit you far beyond the classroom, equipping you to navigate setbacks with greater composure.
examples.trans: 培养情绪韧性将使你在课堂之外也受益匪浅，让你能更从容地应对挫折。

as much as possible.usageZh: 副词短语，通常修饰动词，表示“尽可能多地、尽量”。常与 learn、practice、save、help 等动词搭配使用。

examples.sentence: Please speak English as much as possible in class.
examples.trans: 请在课堂上尽可能多地说英语。

examples.sentence: We should save water as much as possible in our daily life.
examples.trans: 我们在日常生活中应该尽可能多地节约用水。

examples.sentence: Before the exam, I plan to review my notes as much as possible.
examples.trans: 考试前，我打算尽可能多地复习笔记。

examples.sentence: To improve your listening skills, you should expose yourself to authentic English as much as possible.
examples.trans: 为了提高听力，你应该尽可能多地接触地道的英语。

examples.sentence: When conducting research, it is advisable to consult primary sources as much as possible rather than relying solely on summaries.
examples.trans: 做研究时，建议尽可能多地查阅一手资料，而不是仅仅依赖摘要。

examples.sentence: In an era of information overload, discerning readers filter out noise as much as possible to focus on what genuinely matters.
examples.trans: 在信息过载的时代，有辨别力的读者会尽可能多地过滤掉噪音，专注于真正重要的内容。

the more... the better....usageZh: 比较结构，'the + 比较级..., the + 比较级...'，表示一方程度随另一方变化而变化。口语和书面语都常用，可搭配形容词或副词比较级。

examples.sentence: The more you eat, the better you feel.
examples.trans: 你吃得越多，感觉就越好。

examples.sentence: The more water you drink on hot days, the better your body works.
examples.trans: 热天里你喝水越多，身体运转得就越好。

examples.sentence: The more carefully you check your answers, the better your score will be.
examples.trans: 你检查答案越仔细，分数就会越高。

examples.sentence: The more time you invest in learning a new skill, the better you will perform under pressure.
examples.trans: 你投入学习新技能的时间越多，在压力下表现就会越好。

examples.sentence: The more transparent a company is about its decision-making, the better its employees understand the direction they are heading in.
examples.trans: 一家公司在决策过程中越透明，员工就越能理解公司前进的方向。

examples.sentence: The more systematically researchers document their experimental procedures, the better other teams can replicate and validate their findings.
examples.trans: 研究人员越系统地记录实验步骤，其他团队就越能复现并验证他们的发现。

according to.usageZh: 介词短语，后接名词、代词或从句，表示信息来源或依据。常用于引用数据、报告、规则或他人观点，语体偏正式。

examples.sentence: According to my mom, this soup is good for a cold.
examples.trans: 据我妈妈说，这种汤对感冒有好处。

examples.sentence: According to the school notice, the library will close at five today.
examples.trans: 根据学校通知，图书馆今天五点关门。

examples.sentence: According to the survey, most students prefer to study in the morning rather than late at night.
examples.trans: 根据调查，大多数学生更喜欢早上学习，而不是深夜学习。

examples.sentence: According to the data released by the local government, air quality has improved significantly over the past three years.
examples.trans: 根据当地政府发布的数据，过去三年空气质量显著改善。

examples.sentence: According to the terms outlined in the contract, either party may terminate the agreement with thirty days' written notice.
examples.trans: 根据合同中列出的条款，任何一方都可以提前三十天书面通知终止协议。

examples.sentence: According to a longitudinal study spanning two decades, early exposure to a second language correlates with enhanced cognitive flexibility in adulthood.
examples.trans: 根据一项跨越二十年的纵向研究，早期接触第二语言与成年后认知灵活性的增强存在相关性。

leave a decent impression on.usageZh: 动词短语，后接介词 'on' 加某人，表示给某人留下良好、得体的印象。'decent' 在此表示"不错的、体面的"，比 'good' 更含蓄，常用于面试、社交等正式场合。

examples.sentence: Wearing clean clothes can leave a decent impression on your new classmates.
examples.trans: 穿干净的衣服可以给你的新同学留下良好的印象。

examples.sentence: Arriving on time for a party usually leaves a decent impression on the host.
examples.trans: 准时到达聚会通常会给主人留下良好的印象。

examples.sentence: If you listen carefully and ask good questions, you will leave a decent impression on the speaker.
examples.trans: 如果你认真倾听并提出好问题，你会给演讲者留下良好的印象。

examples.sentence: Being well-prepared for the interview is the most reliable way to leave a decent impression on the hiring manager.
examples.trans: 为面试做好充分准备是给招聘经理留下良好印象最可靠的方式。

examples.sentence: Rather than trying to impress with fancy words, focusing on genuine answers tends to leave a more decent impression on the panel.
examples.trans: 与其试图用花哨的言辞打动别人，专注于真诚的回答往往能给评审小组留下更得体的印象。

examples.sentence: Candidates who demonstrate both technical competence and emotional intelligence are far more likely to leave a decent impression on interviewers evaluating long-term potential.
examples.trans: 那些同时展现出技术能力和情商的候选人，更有可能给评估长期潜力的面试官留下良好印象。

make a great first impression.usageZh: 动词短语，通常后接介词 on 加某人或某群体，表示“给……留下良好的第一印象”。多用于面试、社交、职场等正式或半正式场合。

examples.sentence: Wear a clean shirt to make a great first impression at the party.
examples.trans: 穿一件干净的衬衫，在聚会上留下良好的第一印象。

examples.sentence: She smiled and said hello to make a great first impression on her new classmates.
examples.trans: 她微笑着打招呼，给新同学留下良好的第一印象。

examples.sentence: If you arrive on time and speak clearly, you will make a great first impression at the interview.
examples.trans: 如果你准时到达并且说话清楚，你会在面试中留下良好的第一印象。

examples.sentence: Having done thorough research on the company, he was able to make a great first impression during the panel discussion.
examples.trans: 由于对公司做了充分的研究，他在小组讨论中成功留下了良好的第一印象。

examples.sentence: While a firm handshake may help you make a great first impression, it is your genuine interest in the role that leaves a lasting mark.
examples.trans: 虽然有力的握手可能帮你留下良好的第一印象，但真正留下持久印记的是你对这份工作的真诚兴趣。

examples.sentence: Candidates who make a great first impression tend to demonstrate not only professional competence but also a readiness to engage with the team from day one.
examples.trans: 能留下良好第一印象的候选人往往不仅展现出专业能力，还表现出从第一天起就愿意融入团队的态度。

win the heart of.usageZh: 动词短语，后接名词或代词，表示“赢得某人的喜爱或认可”。可用于恋爱、师生、观众、面试官等对象，语体偏正面、感性。

examples.sentence: The little cat won the heart of my grandma with its soft fur.
examples.trans: 这只小猫用柔软的毛赢得了我奶奶的喜爱。

examples.sentence: The new student won the heart of the whole class by helping others every day.
examples.trans: 这位新同学每天帮助别人，赢得了全班同学的喜爱。

examples.sentence: The young singer won the heart of the audience as soon as she began to perform on stage.
examples.trans: 这位年轻歌手一上台表演就赢得了观众的心。

examples.sentence: By patiently listening to every customer's concern, the shop assistant gradually won the heart of the local community.
examples.trans: 通过耐心倾听每位顾客的诉求，这位店员逐渐赢得了当地社区居民的喜爱。

examples.sentence: It was not his eloquence but his consistent honesty that won the heart of the skeptical committee.
examples.trans: 赢得持怀疑态度的委员会认可的，不是他的口才，而是他一贯的诚实。

examples.sentence: A leader who wins the heart of the workforce does so not through authority alone, but through a visible commitment to their well-being and growth.
examples.trans: 能赢得员工真心的领导者，靠的不仅仅是权威，更是对员工福祉与成长的切实投入。

take a quick look at.usageZh: 动词短语，后接名词或代词，表示“快速浏览、看一眼”。常用于请人帮忙检查、翻阅文件或简要了解信息，口语和书面语均可使用。

examples.sentence: Take a quick look at the picture and tell me what you see.
examples.trans: 快速看一下这张图片，告诉我你看到了什么。

examples.sentence: Before you leave the house, take a quick look at the weather report on your phone.
examples.trans: 出门前，快速看一眼手机上的天气预报。

examples.sentence: The teacher asked us to take a quick look at the passage before answering the questions.
examples.trans: 老师让我们在回答问题前快速浏览一下这篇文章。

examples.sentence: Having taken a quick look at the draft, she immediately spotted several inconsistencies in the data.
examples.trans: 快速浏览了草稿后，她立刻发现了数据中的几处不一致。

examples.sentence: Rather than reading the entire report, the manager chose to take a quick look at the executive summary before the meeting.
examples.trans: 经理没有通读整份报告，而是选择在会前快速浏览执行摘要。

examples.sentence: Investors rarely commit funds after merely taking a quick look at a pitch deck; they expect a rigorous demonstration of market potential and risk control.
examples.trans: 投资者很少仅凭快速浏览一份融资演示文稿就投入资金；他们期待看到对市场潜力和风险控制的严谨论证。

last but not least.usageZh: 固定短语，用于列举或演讲的结尾，引出最后一项但强调其重要性不亚于前面各项。常用于正式或半正式场合，如演讲、作文、感谢词。

examples.sentence: Last but not least, I want to thank my mom for the nice lunch.
examples.trans: 最后但同样重要的是，我想感谢妈妈做的美味午餐。

examples.sentence: We need eggs, milk, and last but not least, some bread for breakfast.
examples.trans: 我们需要鸡蛋、牛奶，最后但同样重要的是，早餐还需要一些面包。

examples.sentence: Last but not least, remember to turn off the lights before you leave the lab.
examples.trans: 最后但同样重要的是，离开实验室前记得关灯。

examples.sentence: Last but not least, the school has decided to build a new library that will be open to all students.
examples.trans: 最后但同样重要的是，学校决定建一座新图书馆，向全体学生开放。

examples.sentence: The new policy will reduce costs, improve efficiency, and last but not least, boost employee morale.
examples.trans: 新政策将降低成本、提高效率，最后但同样重要的是，提升员工士气。

examples.sentence: Last but not least, the study highlights the crucial role that consistent sleep patterns play in maintaining long-term cognitive health.
examples.trans: 最后但同样重要的是，该研究强调了规律睡眠模式在维持长期认知健康方面所起的关键作用。

avoid socializing with.usageZh: 动词短语，avoid 后接动名词形式。表示有意避开与某人交往或互动，常用于描述社交习惯、健康建议或心理状态。

examples.sentence: Tom has a cold, so he should avoid socializing with his classmates today.
examples.trans: 汤姆感冒了，所以今天他应该避免和同学们交往。

examples.sentence: If you feel tired after a long week, you don't have to avoid socializing with everyone—just take a short rest.
examples.trans: 如果一周下来你感到疲惫，你不必避免和所有人交往——休息一下就好。

examples.sentence: Doctors often advise patients with a fever to avoid socializing with others until they fully recover.
examples.trans: 医生通常建议发烧的患者在完全康复之前避免与他人交往。

examples.sentence: Some teenagers tend to avoid socializing with their parents, preferring to spend time alone in their rooms.
examples.trans: 一些青少年倾向于避免与父母交往，更喜欢独自待在房间里。

examples.sentence: While it is natural to want some privacy, consistently avoiding socializing with colleagues may harm your professional relationships.
examples.trans: 虽然想要一些隐私是自然的，但长期避免与同事交往可能会损害你的职业关系。

examples.sentence: Individuals who deliberately avoid socializing with peers over an extended period often exhibit higher levels of anxiety and lower self-esteem.
examples.trans: 长期刻意避免与同龄人交往的个体往往表现出更高的焦虑水平和更低的自尊。

bring you down.usageZh: 动词短语，及物，宾语通常是人。表示使某人情绪低落、沮丧或失去信心，常用于劝告、鼓励或描述负面影响的语境。

examples.sentence: Rainy days sometimes bring me down, but a hot cup of tea helps.
examples.trans: 下雨天有时会让我情绪低落，但一杯热茶会好很多。

examples.sentence: Don't let one bad grade bring you down—you can do better next time.
examples.trans: 不要让一次糟糕的成绩让你情绪低落——你下次可以做得更好。

examples.sentence: Negative comments from others can easily bring you down if you care too much about what people think.
examples.trans: 如果你太在意别人的看法，他人的负面评论很容易让你情绪低落。

examples.sentence: Surrounding yourself with people who constantly complain will eventually bring you down without your realizing it.
examples.trans: 身边围绕着不断抱怨的人，最终会在你不知不觉中让你情绪低落。

examples.sentence: Rather than allowing setbacks to bring you down, treat them as opportunities to reassess your approach and grow stronger.
examples.trans: 与其让挫折使你消沉，不如把它们当作重新评估方法并变得更强大的机会。

examples.sentence: Persistent exposure to toxic workplace culture can gradually bring you down, undermining both your productivity and mental well-being.
examples.trans: 长期暴露在有害的职场文化中会逐渐让你情绪低落，同时损害你的工作效率和心理健康。

share with.usageZh: 动词短语。用法：share (something) with somebody，表示“与某人分享某物”。share 后可直接接分享的内容（名词或代词），然后用 with 引出分享的对象。口语和书面语都常用，语气友好。

examples.sentence: I share my lunch with my best friend at school.
examples.trans: 我在学校和最好的朋友分享午餐。

examples.sentence: My sister doesn't like to share her toys with other kids.
examples.trans: 我妹妹不喜欢和其他孩子分享她的玩具。

examples.sentence: When I feel sad, I always share my feelings with my mother first.
examples.trans: 当我感到难过时，我总是先和妈妈分享我的感受。

examples.sentence: She decided to share the good news with her teammates as soon as the meeting ended.
examples.trans: 会议一结束，她就决定把这个好消息分享给队友。

examples.sentence: Rather than keeping the experience to himself, he chose to share it with the entire research group.
examples.trans: 他没有把这段经历藏在心里，而是选择与整个研究小组分享。

examples.sentence: The report highlights that employees who feel comfortable sharing concerns with managers tend to report higher job satisfaction.
examples.trans: 报告强调，那些愿意与管理者分享顾虑的员工往往工作满意度更高。

look for.usageZh: 动词短语。用法：look for + 名词/代词，表示“寻找”。强调寻找的过程，不强调结果。口语和书面语都常用。注意与 find 区分：look for 是“找”的动作，find 是“找到”的结果。

examples.sentence: I am looking for my red pencil case.
examples.trans: 我正在找我的红色铅笔盒。

examples.sentence: We spent the whole afternoon looking for a quiet place to read.
examples.trans: 我们花了整个下午寻找一个安静的地方读书。

examples.sentence: He went to the library to look for some books about space travel.
examples.trans: 他去图书馆找一些关于太空旅行的书。

examples.sentence: Having lost his keys twice this week, he began looking for a more organized way to store them.
examples.trans: 这周已经丢了两次钥匙，他开始寻找一种更有条理的方式来存放它们。

examples.sentence: The company is not merely looking for experienced workers; it is looking for people who can think creatively under pressure.
examples.trans: 这家公司不仅仅在寻找有经验的员工，更在寻找能在压力下创造性思考的人。

examples.sentence: Researchers have been looking for evidence linking sleep quality to long-term memory formation, yet the exact mechanism remains unclear.
examples.trans: 研究人员一直在寻找将睡眠质量与长期记忆形成联系起来的证据，但确切机制仍不清楚。

make you feel.usageZh: 动词短语。用法：make + somebody + feel + 形容词，表示“使某人感到……”。make 后接人称代词宾格或名词，再接 feel 和形容词。注意 feel 后不能接副词，要接形容词。口语和书面语都常用。

examples.sentence: Warm soup makes me feel good on a cold day.
examples.trans: 冷天里热汤让我感觉很好。

examples.sentence: Listening to soft music before bed makes my little brother feel sleepy.
examples.trans: 睡前听轻音乐让我弟弟感到困倦。

examples.sentence: Helping others in need always makes me feel happy and useful.
examples.trans: 帮助有需要的人总是让我感到快乐和有价值。

examples.sentence: Receiving a handwritten letter from an old friend made her feel deeply touched.
examples.trans: 收到老朋友的手写信让她深受感动。

examples.sentence: What makes employees feel valued is not always a higher salary, but genuine recognition of their efforts.
examples.trans: 让员工感到被重视的并不总是更高的薪水，而是对他们努力的真切认可。

examples.sentence: Constant exposure to idealized images on social media can make young people feel inadequate about their own lives.
examples.trans: 持续接触社交媒体上理想化的形象会让年轻人对自己的生活感到不够好。

stay in touch with.usageZh: 动词短语，后接表示人的名词或代词，意为“与某人保持联系”。可用于口语和书面语，常与 keep in touch with 互换。强调持续性的联络状态，而非一次性动作。

family.meaning: 未受影响的；原封未动的

examples.sentence: I stay in touch with my grandma by phone every Sunday.
examples.trans: 我每周日都通过电话和奶奶保持联系。

examples.sentence: My cousin moved to another city, but we still stay in touch with each other online.
examples.trans: 我表姐搬去了另一个城市，但我们仍然在网上保持联系。

examples.sentence: Although we went to different high schools, we managed to stay in touch with each other through letters.
examples.trans: 尽管我们去了不同的高中，我们还是通过书信保持了联系。

examples.sentence: Having worked together for five years, the former colleagues made a sincere effort to stay in touch with one another.
examples.trans: 共事五年之后，这些前同事们真诚地努力保持彼此之间的联系。

examples.sentence: It is often the friends we least expect who stay in touch with us when times get hard, not the ones who promised to.
examples.trans: 在困难时期与我们保持联系的，往往不是那些承诺过的人，而是我们最意想不到的朋友。

examples.sentence: Despite the geographical distance and the demands of their respective careers, the two scientists stayed in touch with each other for over three decades, exchanging ideas that would eventually reshape their field.
examples.trans: 尽管地理距离遥远，且各自事业繁忙，这两位科学家保持了三十多年的联系，交流的思想最终重塑了他们的领域。

a substitute for.usageZh: 名词短语，意为“……的替代品”，for 后接被替代的事物。常用于否定句或表示“无法真正替代”的语境中。可搭配形容词如 good/poor/acceptable 来修饰 substitute。

examples.sentence: Water is not a substitute for milk in this cake recipe.
examples.trans: 在这个蛋糕食谱里，水不能替代牛奶。

examples.sentence: Playing video games is fun, but it is not a substitute for real exercise.
examples.trans: 玩电子游戏很有趣，但它不能替代真正的锻炼。

examples.sentence: The teacher reminded us that watching the film version is not a substitute for reading the original novel.
examples.trans: 老师提醒我们，看电影版本并不能替代阅读原著小说。

examples.sentence: Many parents worry that tablets and smartphones have become a substitute for face-to-face conversation at the dinner table.
examples.trans: 许多家长担心平板电脑和智能手机已经成了餐桌上面对面交谈的替代品。

examples.sentence: No amount of online interaction can serve as a substitute for the trust built through shared physical experience.
examples.trans: 再多的线上互动也无法替代通过共同亲身经历所建立起来的信任。

examples.sentence: While artificial sweeteners are often marketed as a substitute for sugar, long-term studies suggest that they may not be a healthier one after all.
examples.trans: 虽然人工甜味剂常被宣传为糖的替代品，但长期研究表明它们终究未必是更健康的选择。

on a regular basis.usageZh: 介词短语，作频率状语，意为“定期地、经常地”。通常置于句末或动词之后，用于描述习惯性、规律性的动作。比 regularly 更正式一些，常见于书面语和说明性文本。

examples.sentence: My dad goes swimming on a regular basis to keep fit.
examples.trans: 我爸爸定期去游泳来保持健康。

examples.sentence: The school library buys new books on a regular basis so that students always have something fresh to read.
examples.trans: 学校图书馆定期购买新书，这样学生们总有新鲜的书可读。

examples.sentence: If you want to improve your English, you should practice speaking on a regular basis instead of only before exams.
examples.trans: 如果你想提高英语水平，就应该定期练习口语，而不是只在考试前练。

examples.sentence: Volunteers are expected to commit to visiting the elderly residents on a regular basis, as consistency is key to building trust.
examples.trans: 志愿者需要承诺定期探访老年居民，因为持续性是建立信任的关键。

examples.sentence: Unlike sporadic bursts of enthusiasm, exercising on a regular basis yields measurable improvements in both physical and mental health.
examples.trans: 与偶尔爆发的热情不同，定期锻炼能在身心健康两方面都带来可衡量的改善。

examples.sentence: Companies that update their security systems on a regular basis are far less vulnerable to cyberattacks than those that only react after a breach has occurred.
examples.trans: 定期更新安全系统的公司，比那些只在漏洞发生后才有反应的公司，遭受网络攻击的风险要低得多。

be willing to.usageZh: 形容词短语，后接动词原形，表示“愿意做某事”。常用于描述人的态度或选择，口语和书面语都适用。否定形式为 be not willing to，疑问句将 be 动词提前。

examples.sentence: My mom is willing to help me with my homework after dinner.
examples.trans: 我妈妈愿意晚饭后帮我做作业。

examples.sentence: Tom is willing to share his lunch with his classmate who forgot to bring food.
examples.trans: 汤姆愿意和忘带午饭的同学分享他的午餐。

examples.sentence: She is willing to take the early bus so that she can arrive at school on time.
examples.trans: 她愿意坐早班公交车，这样她就能准时到校。

examples.sentence: Not everyone is willing to admit their mistakes, but those who do often earn more respect from others.
examples.trans: 不是每个人都愿意承认自己的错误，但那些愿意承认的人往往能赢得他人更多的尊重。

examples.sentence: He was willing to sacrifice his weekend plans to help his team finish the project before the deadline.
examples.trans: 他愿意牺牲周末的计划来帮助团队在截止日期前完成项目。

examples.sentence: Only when individuals are willing to step out of their comfort zones can they truly discover their hidden potential.
examples.trans: 只有当个人愿意走出舒适区时，他们才能真正发现自己隐藏的潜力。

connect with.usageZh: 动词短语，后接名词或代词作宾语，表示“与某人建立联系”或“与某事物产生共鸣”。with 后接联系的对象，可以是人、群体、文化或抽象概念。口语和书面语均常用。

examples.sentence: I want to connect with my new classmates and make more friends.
examples.trans: 我想和新同学建立联系，交更多朋友。

examples.sentence: Playing basketball together is a great way to connect with people who share the same hobby.
examples.trans: 一起打篮球是和有相同爱好的人建立联系的好方法。

examples.sentence: Reading books allows us to connect with ideas and experiences from people who lived long ago.
examples.trans: 阅读书籍让我们能够与很久以前生活过的人的思想和经历产生联系。

examples.sentence: Social media makes it easier to connect with old friends, but face-to-face communication still matters more for building deep relationships.
examples.trans: 社交媒体让联系老朋友变得更容易，但面对面交流对于建立深厚关系仍然更为重要。

examples.sentence: A skilled interviewer knows how to connect with the audience by telling stories that feel both personal and universal.
examples.trans: 一位熟练的采访者知道如何通过讲述既个人化又具有普遍性的故事来与观众产生共鸣。

examples.sentence: The ability to connect with people from diverse cultural backgrounds has become an essential skill in today's globalized workplace.
examples.trans: 与来自不同文化背景的人建立联系的能力已成为当今全球化职场中的一项必备技能。

grammar.key: The more..., the better... / 越...越...
grammar.title: “越……越……”结构：The more..., the better... 及其拓展（含 the + 比较级 + 主语 + 谓语）
grammar.titleEn: The more..., the better... / The + comparative..., the + comparative...
grammar.usage:
“The more..., the better...”是英语中表示“越……就越……”的核心结构，用来表达两个事物或情况按相同比例变化：前一个“the + 比较级”提出条件，后一个“the + 比较级”说明随之产生的结果。这里的 the 不是冠词，而是副词，表示“到那种程度”。该结构可以连接形容词比较级，也可以连接副词比较级，还可以连接“the + 比较级 + 名词”的形式。

肯定形式中，两个分句都使用“the + 比较级”开头，例如：The harder you work, the more progress you make. 否定形式通常在比较级前加 less，或使用否定意义的比较结构，例如：The less you complain, the happier you feel. 疑问形式较少直接出现，但在口语或书面语中可以通过主句部分构成疑问，例如：Is it true that the more you practice, the better you speak? 实际考试中更常考查陈述句中的语序和比较级形式。

“The more..., the better...”与“more and more”不同：前者强调两个变化之间的因果关系，后者只表示单一事物程度逐渐加深。例如：He runs faster and faster.（他跑得越来越快。）与 The faster he runs, the more tired he becomes.（他跑得越快，就越累。）两者不能混用。此外，该结构与“as...as...”也不同，后者表示同等程度，不表示比例变化。

初中阶段主要掌握“The + 比较级, the + 比较级”的基本形式，常见于“The more, the better.”“The sooner, the better.”等省略句。高中阶段则要求掌握完整句子中的主谓结构、名词性比较级、省略现象以及该结构在书面表达中的高级运用，例如：The more information we gather, the more accurate our conclusion will be. 高中还常考查该结构与倒装、状语从句省略的结合。

易错点一：漏掉第二个 the。不能说 The more you read, better you write. 正确形式应为 The more you read, the better you write. 易错点二：把 the 当成冠词，后面直接接名词，而忽略比较级。例如不能说 The more books you read, the more knowledge. 应说 the more knowledge you gain. 易错点三：两个分句语序混乱，把主语和谓语位置放错。易错点四：在比较级前误加 more，造成双重比较，例如 the more better 是错误的。
forms: The + 比较级 + 主语 + 谓语, the + 比较级 + 主语 + 谓语
The + 比较级 + 名词 + 主语 + 谓语, the + 比较级 + 名词 + 主语 + 谓语
The + 比较级, the + 比较级（省略主语和谓语）
The less + 形容词/副词 + 主语 + 谓语, the less + 形容词/副词 + 主语 + 谓语
The more + 名词 + 主语 + 谓语, the more + 名词 + 主语 + 谓语
The + 比较级 + 主语 + 谓语, the + 比较级（结果部分可省略主语谓语）
notes: 两个分句都必须以“the + 比较级”开头，第二个 the 不可省略，否则句子结构不完整。
the 在此处是副词，不是冠词，后面必须接比较级，不能直接接名词原形。
比较级前不要再加 more 或 most，避免出现 the more better、the most faster 这类双重比较错误。
在高考书面表达中，使用完整主谓结构比只用省略形式更显正式和高级，例如 The more efforts we make, the more likely we are to succeed.
注意语域：口语中常用省略形式如 The sooner, the better.，但正式写作中应尽量补全主语和谓语，使逻辑关系更清晰。

examples.en: The more you practice, the better you will play.
examples.cn: 你练习得越多，就会打得越好。

examples.en: The earlier we leave, the less traffic we will meet.
examples.cn: 我们出发得越早，遇到的交通拥堵就越少。

examples.en: The more expensive the hotel is, the more comfortable the rooms are.
examples.cn: 酒店越贵，房间就越舒适。

examples.en: The more carefully you check your work, the fewer mistakes you will make.
examples.cn: 你检查作业越仔细，犯的错误就越少。

examples.en: The more knowledge we acquire, the more confident we become in expressing our opinions.
examples.cn: 我们获得的知识越多，表达观点时就越自信。

examples.en: The less dependent we are on non-renewable resources, the more sustainable our development will be.
examples.cn: 我们对不可再生资源的依赖越少，我们的发展就越可持续。

exercises.q: ________ you practice, ________ you will play the piano.
exercises.explain: 考查“the + 比较级, the + 比较级”表示“越……就越……”的结构。

exercises.q: The ________ you run, the ________ you will feel.
exercises.explain: 前半句用比较级faster，后半句也要用比较级more tired。

exercises.q: ________ you eat, ________ you will be.
exercises.explain: “越吃越胖”用the more和the fatter，前后都是比较级。

exercises.q: The ________ you get up, the ________ you can catch the bus.
exercises.explain: early的比较级是earlier，easily的比较级是more easily。

exercises.q: ________ you read, ________ you will know.
exercises.explain: 前后都用“the + 比较级”，表示“读得越多，知道得越多”。

exercises.q: The ________ you study, the ________ grades you will get.
exercises.explain: 考查“the + 比较级, the + 比较级”结构，study hard对应better grades。

exercises.q: The ________ you walk, the ________ you will arrive.
exercises.explain: 走得越快，到得越早，前后都用比较级。

exercises.q: The ________ you speak, the ________ others can understand you.
exercises.explain: 说得越慢，别人越能理解你，slowly的比较级是more slowly。

exercises.q: The more you sleep, the more tired you feel. 这句话的意思是“你睡得越多，你就越累”。
exercises.explain: 句子结构正确，表达“睡得越多越累”的意思。

exercises.q: The more you practice English, the better you will speak it. 这句话结构正确。
exercises.explain: “the + 比较级, the + 比较级”结构使用正确。

exercises.q: If you read more books, you will learn more. (用the more...the more改写)
exercises.answer: The more books you read, the more you will learn.
exercises.explain: 将if条件句转换为“the + 比较级, the + 比较级”结构。

exercises.q: If you run faster, you will get there sooner. (用the more...the better改写)
exercises.answer: The faster you run, the sooner you will get there.
exercises.explain: 用比较级结构替换if条件句，表示“越快……越早……”。

exercises.q: If you eat more, you will become fatter. (用the more...the more改写)
exercises.answer: The more you eat, the fatter you will become.
exercises.explain: 将条件句改写为“越……越……”结构。

exercises.q: The more you practice, the best you will be.
exercises.answer: The more you practice, the better you will be.
exercises.explain: 后半句必须用比较级better，不能用最高级best。

exercises.q: More you study, the more you know.
exercises.answer: The more you study, the more you know.
exercises.explain: 第一个比较级前缺少定冠词the。

exercises.q: The ________ you are, the ________ mistakes you will make.
exercises.explain: careful的比较级是more careful，mistakes是可数名词用fewer修饰。

exercises.q: ________ you know about the company, ________ chance you have of getting the job.
exercises.explain: 考查课文原句结构，前后都用比较级。

exercises.q: The ________ you wait, the ________ you will feel.
exercises.explain: long的比较级是longer，impatient的比较级是more impatient。

exercises.q: The ________ you explain, the ________ the students understand.
exercises.explain: clearly的比较级是more clearly，understand用better修饰。

exercises.q: ________ you think about the problem, ________ you will solve it.
exercises.explain: easily的比较级是more easily，与the more搭配。

exercises.q: The ________ you listen to the teacher, the ________ you will understand the lesson.
exercises.explain: carefully的比较级是more carefully，understand用better修饰。

exercises.q: The ________ friends you have, the ________ you will feel.
exercises.explain: 朋友越多越快乐，friends可数用more，happy比较级是happier。

exercises.q: The ________ you drive, the ________ accidents you will have.
exercises.explain: 开车越小心，事故越少，accidents可数用fewer。

exercises.q: The more you practice, the more confident you become. 这句话的意思是“你练习得越多，你就变得越自信”。
exercises.explain: 句子结构和意思都正确，confident的比较级是more confident。

exercises.q: The harder you work, the more successful you will be. 这句话结构正确。
exercises.explain: hard的比较级是harder，successful的比较级是more successful。

exercises.q: If you know more about the company, you will have a better chance of getting the job. (用the more...the better改写)
exercises.answer: The more you know about the company, the better chance you will have of getting the job.
exercises.explain: 将if条件句改写为课文中的“the more...the better”结构。

exercises.q: If you speak more English, you will become more fluent. (用the more...the more改写)
exercises.answer: The more English you speak, the more fluent you will become.
exercises.explain: 将条件句转换为“越……越……”结构，fluent比较级是more fluent。

exercises.q: If you save more money, you will be richer. (用the more...the richer改写)
exercises.answer: The more money you save, the richer you will be.
exercises.explain: 用比较级结构替换if条件句，表示“存钱越多越富有”。

exercises.q: The more you read, the more you will know, and the more you learn, the more places you will go.
exercises.answer: The more you read, the more you will know, and the more you learn, the more places you will go.
exercises.explain: 此句结构完全正确，无需修改，考查对正确结构的辨识。

exercises.q: The more you exercise, the more healthier you become.
exercises.answer: The more you exercise, the healthier you become.
exercises.explain: healthy的比较级是healthier，前面不能再加more。

exercises.q: The ________ you prepare for the interview, the ________ you will perform.
exercises.explain: thoroughly的比较级是more thoroughly，perform用better修饰。

exercises.q: ________ you understand the culture of the company, ________ you will fit in.
exercises.explain: well的比较级是better，easily的比较级是more easily。

exercises.q: The ________ you are about your goals, the ________ you are to achieve them.
exercises.explain: specific和likely的比较级都是前面加more。

exercises.q: ________ you procrastinate, ________ time you will have to finish the project.
exercises.explain: 拖延越多，时间越少，time不可数用less。

exercises.q: The ________ you analyze the data, the ________ conclusions you can draw.
exercises.explain: analyze用副词carefully修饰，conclusions用形容词accurate修饰。

grammar.key: Gerund as Subject / 动名词作主语
grammar.title: 动名词作主语：从基础用法到高中拓展（含不定式对比与主谓一致）
grammar.titleEn: Gerund as Subject: Core Usage and Senior High Extensions
grammar.usage:
动名词作主语是英语中把动作名词化的重要语法手段。其核心结构为“动名词（V-ing）+ 单数谓语动词”，表示一种泛指、抽象或习惯性的活动或状态，而不是某一次具体行为。例如“Swimming is good for your health.”中的 swimming 并不指某一次具体的游泳，而是指游泳这类活动。

肯定句直接以动名词开头，谓语用单数；否定句在动名词前加 not，如“Not getting enough sleep affects your memory.”；疑问句通常借助 it 作形式主语，如“Is it worth spending so much time on this?”。在书面语中，动名词作主语比不定式更常见，语气也更正式、更自然。

动名词作主语与不定式作主语是高中阶段的重要对比点。动名词多表示一般性、习惯性、已知或正在进行的活动；不定式则常表示具体的、一次性的、将来的或带有目的性的动作。例如“Reading widely helps you write better.”强调广泛阅读这一习惯；“To read this report carefully is necessary before the meeting.”则指向会前这一具体任务。高中阶段还常出现“It is no use / no good / a waste of time + doing”等固定句型，这些句型中只能用动名词，不能用不定式。

初中阶段主要要求掌握动名词作主语时谓语用单数，以及常见动名词短语作主语的句子；高中阶段则进一步要求区分动名词与不定式作主语的语义差异、掌握形式主语 it 的句型转换、理解动名词的复合结构（如“His coming late made the teacher angry.”）以及在书面表达中恰当使用动名词作主语来提升表达的正式度和简洁性。

易错点一：动名词作主语时，谓语动词必须用单数，即使动名词短语中包含复数名词也不能用复数谓语。易错点二：不要把动名词作主语与现在分词作状语混淆，前者是名词性功能，后者是修饰功能。易错点三：在“It is no use doing”等固定句型中误用不定式。易错点四：动名词的否定形式 not 要放在动名词之前，而不是之后。
forms: 动名词（V-ing）+ 单数谓语动词：Swimming is good for your health.
否定：Not + 动名词 + 单数谓语动词：Not exercising regularly leads to health problems.
形式主语：It is + 形容词/名词 + 动名词：It is no use crying over spilt milk.
动名词复合结构：形容词性物主代词/名词所有格 + 动名词 + 单数谓语：His arriving late surprised everyone.
固定句型：It is no good / a waste of time / worth + 动名词：It is a waste of time arguing with him.
对比结构：动名词（泛指/习惯） vs 不定式（具体/将来）：Reading widely helps you write better. / To read this report carefully is necessary before the meeting.
notes: 动名词作主语时，谓语动词一律用单数，即使动名词短语中包含复数名词，如“Reading books is my hobby.”中的 is 不能写成 are。
高考书面表达中，适当使用动名词作主语可以提升句式的正式度和简洁性，但不要通篇都用动名词开头，以免句式单调。
在“It is no use / no good / a waste of time / worth”等固定句型中，只能用动名词，不能用不定式，这是高考语法填空和短文改错的常见考点。
动名词的否定形式是“not + 动名词”，not 必须放在动名词之前，如“Not knowing the answer is nothing to be ashamed of.”。
注意动名词作主语与现在分词作状语的语域差异：动名词作主语属于名词性用法，多用于书面语和正式表达；现在分词作状语则多用于描写和叙述，口语中也较常见。

grammar.title: If 第一类条件句：真实条件与主将从现（含祈使句、情态动词及 unless 拓展）
grammar.titleEn: If-Conditional (Type 1): Real Conditions and Present-Future Matching
grammar.usage:
第一类条件句用于表达“在说话人看来很有可能发生或真实存在的条件”，以及在该条件下“将会发生的结果”。其核心结构为：If 从句使用一般现在时，主句使用一般将来时、祈使句或含有情态动词的谓语结构。肯定句如：If you work hard, you will pass the exam. 否定句可在从句或主句中分别否定，如：If he doesn't hurry, he will miss the bus. 疑问句可对主句提问，如：What will you do if it rains tomorrow? 也可对从句提问，但更常见的是主句为疑问形式。

与第二类条件句（If + 过去时，主句 would + 动词原形）相比，第一类条件句表示的条件更真实、更可能实现；第二类则表示假设、不太可能或与现在事实相反的情况。与 unless（= if...not）相比，unless 本身已含否定意义，不能再与否定词连用，如：Unless you hurry, you will be late. 相当于 If you don't hurry, you will be late.

初中阶段主要要求掌握“主将从现”的基本搭配，即 If 从句用一般现在时，主句用 will + 动词原形。高中阶段则进一步拓展到：主句可使用情态动词（can, may, might, should, must 等）表达可能性、建议、义务等语气；主句可使用祈使句表示建议、指令或提醒；从句中可使用现在完成时强调“先完成某条件”，如：If you have finished your homework, you can go out. 此外，高中还要求能在书面表达中灵活使用 unless、as long as、provided that 等替代 if，以提升句式的多样性和正式度。

易错点一：从句中误用 will。第一类条件句中，if 引导的条件状语从句不能用一般将来时，必须用一般现在时表示将来意义。易错点二：主句与从句时态同时用一般现在时，造成“条件”与“结果”关系不清。易错点三：unless 与否定词重复使用，如 Unless you don't work hard 是错误的。易错点四：混淆第一类与第二类条件句，把真实可能的条件误写成与事实相反的假设。
forms: If + 一般现在时，主语 + will/shall + 动词原形
If + 一般现在时，主语 + 情态动词(can/may/might/should/must) + 动词原形
If + 一般现在时，祈使句
If + 一般现在时，主语 + 一般现在时（表示客观规律或习惯性结果）
Unless + 一般现在时，主语 + will/情态动词 + 动词原形（= If...not...）
If + 现在完成时，主语 + 情态动词/祈使句（强调条件先完成）
notes: 高考书面表达中，避免通篇只用 will 主句，可交替使用情态动词或祈使句，使语气更丰富。
在正式语域中，unless 比 if...not 更简洁，但要注意 unless 本身已含否定，不可再与否定词连用。
if 引导的条件状语从句中，即使表达将来意义，也必须用一般现在时，这是高考语法填空和短文改错的高频考点。
当主句表示客观规律或习惯性结果时，主句也可用一般现在时，不要机械套用“主将从现”。
注意区分真实条件（第一类）与假设条件（第二类）：若条件明显与事实相反或几乎不可能实现，应使用第二类条件句。

exercises.explain: 主句用一般将来时提问，构成 Will you help me...?

exercises.explain: 第一类条件句主句可以用祈使句表示建议或命令。

exercises.explain: if 从句中不能用 will，要用一般现在时表示将来。

exercises.explain: 第一类条件句主句可以用情态动词 can 加动词原形。

exercises.explain: if 从句用一般现在时，主语 you 用动词原形。

exercises.explain: if 从句不能用 will，应改为一般现在时 study。

exercises.explain: 第一类条件句主句可以用情态动词 may 表示可能性。

grammar.key: Passive Voice (Present Simple) / 被动语态（一般现在时）
grammar.title: 被动语态（一般现在时）：从基础结构到高中语域拓展
grammar.titleEn: Passive Voice (Present Simple): Core Structures and Senior-Level Extension
grammar.usage:
被动语态的核心作用是调整句子重心，把“动作的承受者”放在主语位置，从而弱化或省略“动作的执行者”。一般现在时的被动语态基本结构为：am/is/are + 过去分词。肯定句中，主语决定 be 动词的形式：I 用 am，he/she/it 及单数名词用 is，we/you/they 及复数名词用 are。否定形式在 be 动词后加 not，如 is not cleaned、are not allowed。疑问形式将 be 动词提到主语前，如 Is English spoken here? 特殊疑问句则在疑问词后接 be 动词，如 Where is tea grown?

与主动语态相比，被动语态更常用于不强调执行者、执行者未知、执行者显而易见或需要突出承受者的语境。例如“The room is cleaned every day”并不关心是谁打扫，而“Candidates are required to wear formal clothes”则把重点放在候选人身上。与 can/must/should 等情态动词连用时，结构变为“情态动词 + be + 过去分词”，如 can be seen、must be finished，这是高中阶段的重要拓展。

初中阶段主要考查一般现在时被动语态的基本构成、主谓一致以及主动句与被动句的转换。高中阶段则进一步要求：在书面语中恰当使用被动语态以增强客观性；理解“be + 过去分词”不一定是被动语态，也可能是系表结构；掌握“get + 过去分词”在口语和非正式语体中的被动含义；并能将被动语态与各种时态、情态动词结合使用。

易错点一：不及物动词没有被动语态，如 happen、appear、disappear、remain 等不能用于被动结构。易错点二：有些动词的过去分词已形容词化，如 interested、excited、tired，它们与 be 连用时表示状态而非被动动作。易错点三：主动语态中省略的宾语在被动语态中必须还原，如主动句“People speak English here”变为被动句时，English 必须作主语，不能写成“Is spoken English here”。易错点四：在高考书面表达中，过度使用被动语态会使文章显得生硬，应结合主动语态交替使用，以保持行文自然。
forms: 肯定式：主语 + am/is/are + 过去分词
否定式：主语 + am/is/are + not + 过去分词
一般疑问式：Am/Is/Are + 主语 + 过去分词？
特殊疑问式：疑问词 + am/is/are + 主语 + 过去分词？
情态动词被动式：主语 + 情态动词 + be + 过去分词
get 型被动（口语/非正式）：主语 + get(s) + 过去分词
notes: 不及物动词（happen、appear、remain 等）不能用于被动语态，高考语法填空和短文改错中常以此为陷阱。
“be + 过去分词”不一定是被动语态，也可能是系表结构，如 He is interested in music 表示状态，而非“被感兴趣”。
在高考书面表达中，被动语态能增强客观性和正式感，但通篇使用会让文章读起来僵硬，应主动与被动交替使用。
“get + 过去分词”可表达被动含义，但多用于口语和非正式语体，高考书面表达中应优先使用 be 型被动。
主动句变被动句时，原句宾语必须作主语，原句主语如需保留，用 by 引出，但高中阶段更强调在不需要执行者时省略 by 短语。

grammar.key: It is + adjective + for sb + to do sth / It is + 形容词 + for 某人 + to do 某事
grammar.title: It is + 形容词 + for sb to do sth 句型：从基础到拓展（含 of 对比、形式主语与语域差异）
grammar.titleEn: It is + adjective + for sb to do sth: Structure, Contrast with 'of', and Advanced Usage
grammar.usage:
本语法点核心结构为“It is + 形容词 + for + 某人 + to do sth”，其中 It 是形式主语，真正的主语是后面的不定式复合结构“for sb to do sth”。该句型用于评价“某人做某事”这件事的性质，而不是评价某人本身。形容词通常描述动作或事件的难易、重要性、必要性、常见性等，如 important, necessary, common, difficult, easy, possible, impossible 等。

肯定句结构为：It is + adj. + for sb + to do sth。否定句在 is 后加 not，即：It is not + adj. + for sb + to do sth。一般疑问句将 is 提到句首：Is it + adj. + for sb + to do sth? 特殊疑问句则在疑问词后接一般疑问句语序，如：Why is it important for students to read widely?

本句型最容易与“It is + 形容词 + of sb + to do sth”混淆。区别在于：用 for 时，形容词评价的是“事情本身”，如 It is difficult for him to finish the task.（完成这项任务这件事很难）；用 of 时，形容词评价的是“人的品质或性格”，如 It is kind of you to help me.（你帮助我，说明你很善良）。能用于 of 句型的形容词通常可以改写为“You are + adj.”，如 kind, nice, clever, foolish, polite, rude, brave, generous 等；而 for 句型中的形容词一般不能直接用来描述人，如不能说“You are important to get enough sleep”。

初中阶段主要要求掌握 for 的基本结构，能区分 for 与 of 的常见搭配，并在单项选择、完成句子中正确使用。高中阶段则进一步要求：1）理解形式主语 It 的句法功能，能将其与不定式作主语的正式表达互相转换，如 To ask questions about the company is common. → It is common for candidates to ask questions about the company.；2）掌握该句型在书面语中的高频使用，尤其是在议论文、说明文和正式信函中引出观点或评价；3）能灵活运用“It is + adj. + for sb + to do sth”与“sb + find(s) + it + adj. + to do sth”等变体进行句型转换；4）注意该句型在语域上的正式程度，口语中更常用“It's + adj. + for sb + to do sth”的缩略形式，而正式写作中常保留完整形式。

易错点一：介词误用。部分学习者看到形容词描述人时仍用 for，如“It is very kind for you to help me”是错误的，应改为 of。判断方法：若形容词能用来直接描述人，则用 of；若形容词描述事情本身，则用 for。

易错点二：漏掉形式主语 It。有些学习者会直接写“Is important for students to study hard”，这是典型错误。英语中不定式作主语且后置时，句首必须有形式主语 It。

易错点三：不定式符号 to 的遗漏。该句型中 to do sth 是不定式，to 不可省略，如“It is important for students study hard”是错误的。

易错点四：与“It is + adj. + that 从句”混淆。部分学习者在该用 that 从句时误用 for sb to do sth，如“It is important for students that they study hard”虽然语法上可接受，但不如“It is important for students to study hard”简洁自然；反之，当主语不明确或需要完整从句时，不宜强行使用 for sb to do sth。
forms: 肯定式：It is + adj. + for sb + to do sth
否定式：It is not + adj. + for sb + to do sth
一般疑问式：Is it + adj. + for sb + to do sth?
特殊疑问式：疑问词 + is it + adj. + for sb + to do sth?
对比结构：It is + adj. + of sb + to do sth（形容词描述人的品质）
变体结构：sb + find(s) + it + adj. + to do sth
notes: 高考书面语中，该句型常用于引出观点或评价，注意保持正式语域，避免在正式作文中过度使用缩略形式“It's”。
判断 for 还是 of 的关键：把形容词放到人前面，若逻辑通顺则用 of，如“You are kind”成立，故用 of；若不通顺则用 for，如“You are important”不成立，故用 for。
该句型中 It 不可省略，也不能换成 This 或 That。形式主语 It 只起语法作用，不指代具体事物。
在高考语法填空或短文改错中，常考查不定式符号 to 的缺失或介词 for/of 的误用，需结合形容词性质判断。
注意该句型与“It is + adj. + that 从句”的语域差异：for sb to do sth 更简洁，常用于主语明确且动作具体时；that 从句则更正式，适合主语不明确或需要完整陈述时。

grammar.key: Present Perfect Tense / 现在完成时
grammar.title: 现在完成时：从“过去—现在”的桥梁到高中进阶辨析（含 since/for、与一般过去时、完成进行时对比）
grammar.titleEn: Present Perfect Tense: Bridging Past and Present
grammar.usage:
现在完成时的核心结构是“have/has + 过去分词”。它不单纯描述过去，而是站在“现在”回望过去，表达两类核心意义：一是过去动作对现在造成的影响或结果，如“I have lost my key.”（钥匙丢了，现在进不了门）；二是从过去持续到现在的动作或状态，常与 since、for、so far、up to now、recently 等连用，如“She has worked here since 2020.”。

肯定句用“主语 + have/has + 过去分词”，否定句在 have/has 后加 not，疑问句把 have/has 提到主语前。例如：He has finished. / He has not finished. / Has he finished? 注意 have/has 是助动词，否定和疑问都靠它完成，不能再用 do/does/did。

与一般过去时对比：一般过去时只陈述过去某时发生的动作，与现在无关，常与 yesterday、last week、in 2019 等明确的过去时间连用；现在完成时则强调与现在的联系，不能与这些“纯过去时间”连用。例如“I saw the film yesterday.”（只说明昨天看了）与“I have seen the film.”（强调现在知道内容或不想再看）。

初中阶段主要掌握“have/has + 过去分词”的基本形式，以及 for + 时间段、since + 时间点的持续用法。高中阶段则要进一步理解：现在完成时在新闻报道、学术语篇中的“结果/影响”功能；与 already、yet、just、ever、never、recently、lately 等副词的搭配；以及“It/This is the first time that + 现在完成时”等固定句型。

易错点：一是把 have/has 当作实义动词“有”，在疑问和否定中误加助动词；二是把一般过去时和现在完成时混用，尤其是出现 yesterday、ago 等词时仍用现在完成时；三是忘记过去分词的不规则变化；四是忽略“have been to”与“have gone to”的区别——前者表示“去过某地（已回来）”，后者表示“去了某地（还没回来）”。
forms: 肯定句：主语 + have/has + 过去分词
否定句：主语 + have/has + not + 过去分词
一般疑问句：Have/Has + 主语 + 过去分词?
持续用法：主语 + have/has + 过去分词 + for + 时间段 / since + 时间点
固定句型：It/This is the first time (that) + 主语 + have/has + 过去分词
与副词搭配：主语 + have/has + already/just/ever/never/not...yet + 过去分词
notes: 高考书面表达中，现在完成时常用于开头引入背景或总结影响，如“In recent years, great changes have taken place in...”，避免通篇只用一般现在时。
在新闻报道和学术语域中，现在完成时用来引出“截至目前已发生的事”，常与 recently、so far、to date 搭配，体现客观性和时效性。
注意“have been to”与“have gone to”的语域差异：前者可用于日常和书面语，后者多用于口语，且主语不能是第一人称。
在正式书面语中，避免把现在完成时与 yesterday、last year、two days ago 等明确的过去时间状语连用；如必须表达过去时间，改用一般过去时。
高考语法填空常考“since + 过去时间点/一般过去时从句”与现在完成时主句的搭配，注意 since 从句用一般过去时，主句用现在完成时。

exercises.q: By the end of last month, the research team ______ all the data they needed.

exercises.q: Never before ______ such a rapid change in public health awareness.
